n: A hymn of praise framed by the same line at beginning and end. God’s name is majestic throughout the earth, and his glory is set above the heavens.

f.g: “LORD” is Jehovah (YHWH); “Lord” is Adonai, meaning master or sovereign.

n: God uses the praises of little children to silence his enemies — strength from the weakest. Jesus quoted this when children praised him in the temple.

f.w: Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings

n: David gazes at the night sky — moon and stars crafted by God’s fingers, as an artisan crafts fine work.
Compared with all that, why would God care about mere humans? Yet he does — he remembers and visits us. Moses asked a similar question after his vision.

f.w: What is man, that thou art mindful of him?

n: God made humans only a little lower than divine beings and crowned them with glory and honor. Latter-day Saints see here our divine nature as children of God.

f.w: a little lower than the angels
f.g: Hebrew ’elohim — can mean God or divine beings; the Greek Old Testament reads “angels.”

f.w: crowned him with glory and honour

n: God gave humanity stewardship over his creations, putting everything under their feet. Hebrews applies this ultimately to Christ.

f.g: Stewardship and responsible rule, not exploitation.

f.w: thou hast put all things under his feet

n: Domestic animals — sheep and cattle — and wild animals too.
Birds, fish, and every creature that travels the ocean’s paths.
The psalm closes by repeating its opening: Lord, how majestic is your name in all the earth!

f.w: how excellent is thy name in all the earth!
